title: Pain Management in Burned Patients Treated with Bromelain-Based Enzymatic Debridement
content: Background: Bromelain-based enzymatic debridement is a treatment for deep partial and full thickness burns. It is a painful procedure that requires anaesthesia techniques. However, there is limited information on the best strategy to guarantee adequate pain control. Objective: To describe the anaesthetic strategy in patients treated with bromelain-based enzymatic debridement after burn injury. Methods: We performed an observational retrospective study by recording data from the clinical records of burned patients treated with bromelain-based enzymatic debridement. Patients admitted to the Burn Unit of Vall d´Hebron University Hospital between January 2015 and December 2019 were included. Results: We enrolled 112 patients that met the inclusion criteria. The mean burned total body surface area (TBSA) was 10.7% ± 11.34 and the median Abbreviated Burn Severity Index (ABSI) was 5 (2–12). The most frequently burned and treated areas were the upper limbs (73%), followed by the lower limbs (30%) and abdomen (8%). Regional anaesthesia was the most used technique, accounting for 96% of the cases. Axillary blockage was performed in 47% of the patients, with a continuous catheter being placed in 31% of them. In the next 48 hours after bromelain-based enzymatic debridement, 61% of the patients had controlled pain. In 12.5% of the cases, opioids were used for pain relief after the procedure, and in 2.7% of the cases, the anaesthesia technique was repeated. There were no differences in pain control when single nerve block was compared with catheter placement (p = 0.809). Complications appeared in nine patients and included hypotension, nausea and urinary retention. Conclusions: Bromelain-based enzymatic debridement is a painful procedure that requires advanced and specialized anaesthesia management. Regional anaesthesia techniques are a feasible and safe strategy for pain control. Optimal analgesia in the first 48 hours is still a challenge in these patients.
